results.strategy_description:
The Broad Reach Master Fund aims to capture the extraordinary alpha available in Emerging Markets by pursuing macro opportunities globally in countries and assets often overlooked by mainstream managers and indices.  The team employs discretionary and systematic investment processes, with specific strategies designed to target specific alpha streams.  By layering different sources of alpha, the team believes it can deliver differentiated, uncorrelated returns through time.

At the core, a systematic process applies momentum and carry signals across more than 45 countries in FX, rates, credit, equities, and commodities.  This effectively delivers and risk manages capital around the world, harnessing the breadth of positive and negative trends across EM, while also harvesting the universe's abundant carry.  These two distinct return streams produce a highly diversified base to the portfolio.

In turn, the discretionary team focuses on generally less efficient assets, with the aim of adding uncorrelated themes with the potential for outsized returns.  Specifically, the team aims to profit from significant macro events or dislocations (eg sovereign defaults, downgrades, or devaluations) or in less efficient EM assets (eg frontier markets or EM HY credit).  The team may also look for meaningful thematic shifts at the country or asset class level. 

In combination, the systematic and discretionary processes provide a flexible framework to capture different themes in different asset classes and geographies through time.

results.management_company_description:
Tresidor is a London-based alternative credit manager focused on making research-led investments across the full spectrum of tradeable European credit. Tresidor was founded in 2018 by CIO Michael Phelps, the former Head of European Fundamental Credit for BlackRock, where he managed ~$35bn in European credit investments. Michael has over 20 years experience investing in credit markets, utilising the same disciplined fundamental research process that drives Tresidor’s performance. 

Tresidor manages over $2.5bn firmwide AUM for a diversified international institutional investor base, and offers investors a choice of two fundamental European credit strategies; a diversified long/short credit fund "TECF" (which hard-closed for a second time in July 2023, after reopening in January 2023) and a long-only opportunistic distressed credit fund "TECOF", which remains open.

Tresidor has a 24-strong team, including 14 investment professionals, the majority of whom have previously worked with Michael, creating strong continuity of people as well as of process. We are equally committed to our institutional-grade non-investment team and infrastructure, led by CEO Edgar Senior, who has 20 years of experience across credit and hedge funds.
results.strategy_description:
Status: Hard-closed from 01/07/23, but re-opening for limited capacity and a limited period from 30/06/26.

The Tresidor Europe Credit Fund ("TECF") offers investors access to an actively managed portfolio of research-based long and short European credit opportunities, selected by our CIO across the full tradeable credit spectrum, including leveraged, investment grade, asset-backed, distressed and sovereign credit, and utilising bonds, loans, convertibles, credit derivatives, options and stocks. 

We invest across three sub-strategies (Long/short Credit; Event-Driven Credit & Distressed; Diversified Credit), building the portfolio bottom-up using disciplined research-driven credit selection so that neither we nor our investors have to rely on lower-hit-rate top-down market-timing across or within verticals. 

TECF focuses on generating returns from intelligently diversified credit risk, and thus seeks to hedge exposure to interest rate or FX fluctuations, allowing investors to profit from credit-orientated opportunities without needing to time interest rate moves or credit beta.
results.region_exposure_description: The strategy focuses on issuers that have a material portion of operations in, and/or that are headquartered in, developed Europe. Opportunistic exposure to issuers from other developed markets, where consistent with the fund’s mandate and the research team’s expertise, may also be included.
results.share_class_additional_details: Although we invest actively across both publicly listed companies and privately held company, we generally prefer credit instruments that are tradeable and can benefit from a price signal. However, we will hold private equity following restructurings.

The Tresidor Europe Credit Opportunities Fund (“TECOF”) offers investors access to a concentrated long-only portfolio of research-based stressed, distressed and dislocated credit investments sourced from across Developed Europe traded credit markets. 

TECOF seeks to provide through-the-cycle exposure to high-IRR-potential opportunistic credit, using bottom-up fundamental research to rotate name-by-name between stressed/performing credit and re-org/distressed opportunities, as the market environment evolves. 

TECOF doesn't leverage or short, hence typically has 90-100% exposure to a portfolio of high-return-potential bonds and loans, including both performing and distressed issuers, plus other opportunistic corporate exposure such as post-reorg equity. Individual positions typically have at least these characteristics: >15% IRR potential even in the base case underwriting scenario; the ability to build fundamental edge through research; asymmetric upside potential relative to downside risk; and definable downside that our underwriting can quantify.

results.management_company_description: Graham Capital Management, L.P. (“Graham”) is an alternative investment manager founded in 1994 by Kenneth G. Tropin. Specializing in discretionary and quantitative macro strategies, Graham is dedicated to delivering strong, uncorrelated returns across a wide range of market environments.  As one of the industry’s longest-standing global macro and trend-following managers, Graham remains committed to innovation, evolving its strategies through a robust investment, technology, and operational infrastructure. Graham harnesses the synergies between its discretionary and quantitative trading businesses to offer a broad suite of complementary alpha strategies, each built on the principles of thoughtful portfolio construction, active risk management, and diversification by design. Graham invests significant proprietary capital alongside its clients – including global institutions, endowments, foundations, family offices, sovereign wealth funds, investment management advisors, and qualified individual investors – reinforcing alignment of interests across all strategies.
results.strategy_description: Graham Quant Macro (“GQM”) is a directional, long and short strategy that utilizes fundamental and price-based indicators to establish return forecasts across global interest rates, foreign exchange, stock indices and commodities. The strategy incorporates a variety of sub-models that generate macro fundamental forecasts, assess yield and earnings differentials, compare current valuations relative to historic fair value, and analyze directional price trends across markets. Quantitative risk management and portfolio construction techniques are used to diversify risk across the portfolio and enhance risk-adjusted returns. Historically, the average holding period has been approximately eight to ten weeks, although the sub-models will make daily adjustments to positions. The strategy is designed to have low correlation to traditional markets and other alternative strategies and has the potential to provide significant portfolio diversification benefits.

results.strategy_description: Tactical Trend is a dynamic, trend-based strategy comprised of multiple sub-models. The strategy gradually buys and sells based on a number of factors, including price, volatility, and length of time a position has been held. Tactical Trend includes trend-following models that trade based on an intermediate- to long-term time horizon as well as adaptive models, which adjust their behavior, speeding up and slowing down depending on the prevailing market conditions via a feedback mechanism. The holding period for the underlying models generally ranges from a few weeks to months. Historically, the average holding period for the strategy has been approximately six to eight weeks, although the sub-models will make daily adjustments to underlying positions at the market level based on both price activity and market volatility. This strategy trades a broad range of markets, including global interest rates, foreign exchange, global stock indices, and commodities.

results.strategy_description:

The bottom-up approach, which attributes to approximately 80% of the team’s research time, applies our on the ground due diligence with our local investment team. We use our proprietary fundamental research framework to understand our targeted companies’ business model, competitive advantage, management quality and governance, capital allocation capabilities, their earnings and cash flow growth over a three-to-five-year investment horizon. The research process will generate a targeted valuation based on multiples as well as cash flow forecast, which allows the team to work out the intrinsic value of the company and its potential upside. 

The top-down and thematic process represents approximately 20% of our research time. The target is to find economies and industries with positive tailwinds and healthy outlooks and be cautious on those regions and industries with regulatory headwinds, in an effort to prioritize the whole research team’s research capacity.

with bottom-up research to identify leading companies with proven, transparent management 
teams within the investable universe.

results.management_company_description:
Silver Point Capital, L.P. (“Silver Point”, the “Firm”, "we") was founded in 2002 by Edward Mulé and Robert O’Shea, both previously partners at Goldman Sachs (“Goldman”), where together they built and co-headed numerous global credit businesses for the firm. 

Upon departing from Goldman, Mr. Mulé and Mr. O’Shea partnered to establish Silver Point in 2002 to replicate the credit businesses that they had built and managed while at Goldman. The Founders’ vision for Silver Point was to build a world-class private investment firm that would specialize in investing in credit and special situations opportunities.  They believed that they could leverage their experience and expertise to build a global credit investing business that would seek to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns across credit cycles for its investors.

Today, the Firm manages approximately $45 billion in investable assets across synergistic credit strategies, comprising (1) opportunistic credit and special situations funds, which include an evergreen global special situations investing strategy focused on publicly traded credit markets (the “Flagship Hedge Funds”) managing $13 billion in investable assets, (2) a dislocation drawdown strategy (the “Dislocation Drawdown Funds”) managing $7 billion in investable assets,  (3) a performing middle market lending strategy (our “Direct Lending Strategy”) managing $17 billion in investable assets; and (4) a liquid performing credit business managing approximately $8 billion.
results.strategy_description: Silver Point’s Flagship Hedge Funds invest in global credit, distressed and special situations investments throughout the credit cycle. The Funds target investments which are believed to be mispriced typically due to corporate stress/distress, excessive leverage, bankruptcy and other complex situations. The Funds will take an active role in driving investment processes, including restructurings, liquidations and other event-oriented situations by frequently assuming leadership roles in steering, ad hoc and other creditor committees. Often, the Funds also assume a leadership role post-bankruptcy, seeking to work with companies and management teams to implement changes to create value. The Funds employ a deeply analytical, fundamentally-driven bottom-up approach to investing and invest across a variety of industries, geographies, capital structures and market capitalizations. With a mandate to invest throughout a cycle, the Funds have a deep commitment to protecting capital through active management of gross and net exposures based on views of macro risks and market valuations.
results.region_exposure_description:
The Funds have a global mandate. While Silver Point has experience pursuing investment and restructuring processes in over 50 jurisdictions globally, the majority of the portfolio tends to be in North America, given North America has the largest leveraged credit markets and the strongest debtor / creditor laws. We also have significant exposure to Western Europe and have historically had exposure to other regions including Europe, Asia, South America and others.

The strength of creditor laws, process risks, and jurisdictional risks will all impact both risk adjusted and relative returns and will be taken into account when evaluating positions. Ultimately, the geographic breakdown of the Fund will be purely opportunistic and will leverage our experience and expertise in global distressed investing.

results.portfolio_additional_details:
The Funds have a particular focus on companies and/or instruments that we believe are mispriced, stressed, distressed, overleveraged and/or are going through restructurings, bankruptcies or other complex situations. The Fund targets opportunities where it can play an active role in driving restructurings by leading creditor committees, as well as devote significant time on the backend improving these companies. The Funds will invest in both middle market and large companies opportunistically across geographies and industries, assessing the best risk adjusted as well as relative value investments. The Funds’ portfolios will likely be primarily invested in (i) senior secured debt, or in unsecured debt with secured debt characteristics purchased through distressed and liquidation trades; (ii) loans and securities of companies undergoing bankruptcy or other in or out of court restructurings; (iii) dislocated credit trading at prices below what we believe to be its fundamental value; (iv) rescue financings; (v) opportunistic stressed / event-driven loans and securities; as well as (vi) post-restructured equity positions, typically in names where we have taken an active role in driving the restructuring process and anticipate taking an active role in further unlocking value at the company post-restructuring. Although we invest across the capital structure from senior secured debt to equity, we have historically been biased towards investing in senior secured debt or unsecured debt with secured debt characteristics (liquidations) given the attractive risk adjusted return profile of these instruments. These instruments tend to have reduced market risk and downside protection. As mentioned, we target positions where we believe we can take an active role in driving events, wield outsized influence during a restructuring, and work constructively with management teams’ post-bankruptcy in order to create value. We believe that being active in an investment often increases return, shortens duration, and decreases risk.

The Fund typically has 60-80 meaningful long positions. The Fund does not employ leverage as part of its investment strategy and gross long exposure typically ranges from approximately 80-105% of long NAV. The Firm seeks to actively manage its exposures, market technicals and risks. The Firm evaluates its net exposure on a daily basis and makes modifications as the environment and opportunity set evolve.

results.management_company_description:
Mycor Capital is a credit hedge fund firm that was founded by Dan Allen (ex-Anchorage) and Josh Samuelson (ex-PointState).

Our flagship long/short credit fund (the L/S Credit Fund) launched in July 2023 and employs a strategy focused on performing, liquid credit (primarily HY, bank loans, some structured credit, IG, preferreds/converts). The strategy targets low double digit net returns in the present environment, on a relatively low volatility and beta profile.

We also manage a long only version of the strategy (the Liquid Credit Fund) which launched in September 2023. This fund employs a more diversified version of the long book of the hedge fund with some parameters around rating, duration, etc. and offers monthly liquidity and a flat management fee.

Mycor's senior investment team, also including Jack Franke (ex-PointState), Matt Knopman (ex-Anchorage), and Ju-Lie Bell (ex-Anchorage), has over 100 years of cumulative investment experience in various market environments.
results.strategy_description:
Mycor's core strategy combines a rigorous credit underwriting process with a robust macro framework to build a portfolio that invests in credit instruments across the rating spectrum and duration continuum.

The long only Liquid Credit Fund aims to invest in credits that have downside protection and substantial free cash flow generation. We approach portfolio construction with a macro framework that tactically shifts exposure across the portfolio, optimizing for credit quality and yield.

This product aims to offer investors an actively managed long only portfolio that dynamically shifts allocations to optimize for duration, quality, and returns. A complete solution to the performing credit asset class continuum with the ability to access structured credit and leverage loans without longer term lock-ups. The investment team has a long history of working together at different institutions, deploying billions of dollars of capital across various credit strategies.

results.name: BSF Global Event Driven Fund
results.management_company_description: BlackRock is a provider of global investment management services. As of December 2024, BlackRock managed $11.60 trillion across equity, fixed income, alternatives, multi-asset, and cash management strategies for institutional and retail clients. Through BlackRock Solutions ("BRS"), the firm provides risk management and advisory services that combine capital markets expertise with internally-developed systems and technology. Today, BlackRock is a global asset and risk manager, serving many of the world's largest companies, pension funds, foundations, and public institutions as well as millions of individual investors globally.
results.strategy_description: The Fund seeks to generate superior risk-adjusted returns by exploiting a range of transformative corporate events. The investment team employs a fundamentally driven investment process focused on identifying investments that have a sufficiently defined catalyst path. Investments span a broad spectrum of both hard and soft catalysts including, for example, announced mergers and acquisitions, company offers, spin-offs and split-offs, financial/strategic restructuring, management changes, synergistic acquisitions, as well as other transformative events. The Fund invests in equities and credit. The investment approach is driven by bottom up, deep fundamental and strategic analysis, with an emphasis on idea differentiation and a focus away from trafficked hedge fund names. Other key elements include effective risk management, hedging strategies, and leverage. In particular, the investment team's ability to isolate an event through a discrete hedging process is core to the investment philosophy. Merger investments are fully hedged to the spread by going long the target and short the acquirer as dictated by the terms of the merger agreement. For soft catalyst investments, investment-level hedges are determined through a combination of fundamental, statistical, and prompt shock analysis, allowing each investment to be hedged with a tailored basket of securities that minimize risks not core to the investment thesis. In selecting hedges, we seek to include securities which we believe will also generate alpha (e.g., other companies that we believe may underperform on a relative basis) and as much as practicable, we focus on individual hedges in lieu of reliance on broader market indices. This disciplined hedging methodology and sophisticated risk controls at both the position and portfolio level are designed to result in a return profile uncorrelated to equity and credit markets.
results.region_exposure_description: The Fund invests in global developed markets (typically U.S. ~60-80%, international ~20-40%), driven by the bottom-up opportunity set across the catalyst spectrum. Portfolio construction is a continuous process, with the team constantly analyzing the impact of new ideas and information on the portfolio as a whole. The approach is flexible, varying through market and economic cycles to position the portfolio appropriately. Geographical concentration will be actively monitored as part of the team’s risk management process.

results.strategy_description:
BlackRock Credit Alpha is a special situations credit fund focused on generating idiosyncratic alpha with low correlation to broader markets. The fund invests in event-driven and/or complex situations across levered capital structures; the investment process emphasizes a deep fundamental underwrite to build a high conviction portfolio, where the top 10 names typically represent 40 – 50% of risk. BCA has an all-weather strategy designed to perform across the credit cycle and will lean into stressed/distressed situations around market dislocations; security selection and dynamic hedging create idiosyncratic exposure with downside management. The fund combines the benefits of a specialized approach with the resources and scale of the BlackRock platform.

results.strategy_description: The Fund aims to provide a positive (absolute) return, regardless of market conditions, over any 12-month period. A positive return is not guaranteed over this or any time period and, particularly over the shorter term, the Fund may experience periods of negative returns. Consequently your capital is at risk. The Fund seeks to achieve its objective by employing a diverse range of investment strategies (as further outlined below), through investing and taking long and short positions in equities and equity related instruments of companies throughout the world, through investment grade and non-investment grade fixed income securities (including government bonds, convertible bonds and contingent convertible bonds), and through their associated financial derivative instruments (such as options, futures, swaps (such as total return swaps, credit default swaps, interest rate swaps, dividend swaps, correlation swaps, variance swaps, volatility swaps and contracts for difference) and warrants). The Fund may also gain indirect exposure to commodities using i) eligible Transferable Securities, ii) units/shares of eligible collective investment schemes, exchange traded funds, and/or iii) derivatives whose underlying assets consist of eligible Transferable Securities or commodity indices. The Fund may also invest in other eligible collective investment schemes and exchange traded funds. Long positions may be held through a combination of direct investment and/or derivative instruments, whilst the short positions are achieved entirely through derivative instruments. The use of derivatives is extensive and forms an important part of the investment strategy. The Fund is a multi-asset global portfolio. Allocations will be made at the Investment Manager’s discretion and the Fund need not be invested in all asset classes at any one time. It follows an unconstrained investment approach, with no regional or sector constraints. In addition, in seeking to implement the Fund's investment strategy, manage market exposure and ensure that the Fund remains sufficiently liquid to cover obligations arising from its derivative positions, a substantial proportion of the Fund’s assets may at any time consist of cash, near cash, deposits and/or Money Market Instruments. Where the Fund uses total return swaps (underlyings including single names, baskets, indices, baskets of indices (including eligible commodity indices) and convertibles), the purpose is to either provide a hedge against underlying exposure/risk within the Fund’s holdings or to provide synthetic exposure on a limited basis to underlying securities which the Fund may otherwise invest in directly. More particularly, in case the underlying of a total return swap consists in a basket of securities or in a basket of indices, the Investment Manager may exercise discretion over the holding weights of each of the underlying securities or indices in the basket. For the avoidance of doubt, such a basket rebalancing shall not be considered to constitute a benchmark administration but shall form part of the Investment Manager’s discretionary management activities. The types of assets used will be of a type which is consistent with the Fund’s investment objective and policy. Please see Appendix 2 for the maximum and expected exposures to total return swaps, including further details on the underlying instruments and rationales of usage. The Fund may invest up to 20% of its net assets in contingent convertible bonds (Cocos). The Fund may also invest up to 10% of its net assets in distressed debt securities. Please see Appendix 3 – Risk Factors for further information on the risks associated with Cocos and distressed securities. The Fund may invest in companies of any size, including smaller capitalization companies. The Fund will not exercise significant influence over the management of any issuing body.

DTP has delivered attractive risk-adjusted returns since its inception and provides a unique proposition in terms of its track record and the underlying philosophy. DTP's track record is characterized by convexity and positive skew, low correlation to the major asset classes and other hedge fund styles, and strong returns during periods of market stress.

DTP trades futures, forwards and swap markets globally across multiple asset classes, applying an active and adaptive trend strategy. Although DTP’s trading tools are fueled only by prices set in the individual markets traded, the program is geared towards capturing the broader underlying trends. The goal is to be sizably positioned in different trends, with a balanced risk allocation across the factors driving current trends.

results.management_company_description:
Ellington Management Group is an investment and advisory firm dedicated to generating attractive risk-adjusted total returns for our investors. Our core competencies include developing and implementing fixed income relative value strategies based on our deep expertise in diversified credit, mortgage prepayment, and interest rates markets. Ellington’s credit investment capabilities include residential and commercial mortgage-backed securities, unsecuritized mortgage and consumer loans, and corporate debt markets.

Ellington’s approximately $19 billion in assets under management include multi-investor funds, managed accounts, and two publicly traded vehicles, Ellington Credit Company (NYSE: EARN) and Ellington Financial Inc. (NYSE: EFC). The Firm currently offers products based on its multi-sector credit strategies, prepayment and related relative value strategies, as well as long-only and traditional mandates. 

Ellington devotes significant operational resources to research and analytics, risk management, information infrastructure, trade execution, legal, compliance, and back office functions. The Firm has offices in New York, Connecticut and London.

Michael Vranos and five other partners founded Ellington in December of 1994. Prior to forming Ellington, five of the founding partners constituted the nucleus of Kidder Peabody’s MBS trading and research group, and the sixth was co-head of CMO trading at Lehman Brothers.
results.strategy_description:
• The strategy seeks to generate attractive yields through a core structured credit portfolio, with a low beta to broader credit markets.
• Utilizes Ellington's models and analytic tools to seek alpha through security selection, in addition to employing an active trading approach, aiming to capture bid-offer spread within its focus markets. 
• Invests in assets across the securitized credit spectrum, with a focus on non-agency RMBS, CMBS, CLOs, and ABS. Within those markets, the fund specifically focuses on assets with risk profiles that are typically more attractive than implied by their ratings. 
• A large portion of the fund’s securitized assets have floating rate coupons and exposure to real assets such as housing, characteristics that position the fund well across a variety of macroeconomic scenario including the current inflationary environment.
 • The Fund targets SOFR +4% over a full market cycle.

results.management_company_description:
Polus Capital Management (“Polus”) is an investment management firm specialising in alternative credit strategies. Polus invests across the capital structure and liquidity spectrum, focusing on three complementary strategies: Leveraged Credit, Special Situations and Structured Credit. 

These strategies are pursued through a range of investment vehicles designed for an institutional investor base including pension funds, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, funds of funds and family offices.
results.strategy_description:
The absolute return strategy seeks to capture extreme disconnects between price and intrinsic value on both longs and shorts to deliver strong risk-adjusted returns in all market environments. Longs generally target opportunistic, stressed or distressed senior debt trading at a significant discount to par, collateralized by hard assets or other tangible value, often requiring legal expertise to drive a process and catalyse a repricing. Shorts generally target subordinated debt of fundamentally fragile, highly levered companies with a high probability of default and low expected recovery. The portfolio construction framework aims to take advantage of inflection points in the market with a view to generating strong returns in normal environments and exceptional returns in dislocated or recessionary environments. The strategy has a European bias with geographic exposure generally expected to be 70% Europe / 30% RoW. 

Polus’ Special Situations team comprises 15 investment professionals who have spent their careers focused on opportunistic, stressed and distressed debt. The Special Situations team has access to 26 additional investment professionals from Polus’ Leveraged Credit and Structured Credit teams.
results.region_exposure_description:
Longs are generally heavily weighted towards Europe due to the sourcing and legal expertise in the region. 
Shorts seek out pockets globally of high corporate leverage, weak capital structures, etc.
The strategy is designed to be opportunistic across geographies in search of the best alpha-generating investments

results.strategy_description: We seek to maintain a diversified portfolio with low net exposure across our portfolio of strategies and often within the investments within each strategy. The fund targets an annualized risk profile of 6-9% and beta in the range of -.2 to + .2. We integrate risk management into the analysis of each investment and apply it at the aggregate portfolio level. The Firm looks at risk control through several lenses. Volatility and VAR measure the correlated as well as the idiosyncratic portions of risk through a well specified factor model. Similarly, every security in the portfolio has a sensitivity to the overall market returns. The Firm is primarily trading US securities; therefore, all risk (equity/derivative/credit) is brought back to equity equivalents then beta-adjusted to the S&P 500 Index. Concentration risk embedded in single name exposures is measured by dollar value exposures as well as “zero-shot” scenarios in which security values go to zero. We target single name exposure of no more than 7.5%.
